facts.statement: Thalassomedon is a genus of plesiosaur named by Welles in 1943, derived from Greek words meaning "sea lord".
facts.quote: Thalassomedon (from Greek, thalassa, "sea" and Greek, medon, "lord" or "ruler", meaning "sea lord") is a genus of plesiosaur, named by Welles in 1943.

facts.statement: Thalassomedon is one of the largest elasmosaurids, with an estimated length of 10.86 to 11.95 meters and a mass of 4.4 to 6.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: Thalassomedon is among the largest elasmosaurids, with an estimated body length of 10.86 - 11.95 m long and body mass of 4.4 - 6.8 MT.

facts.statement: Thalassomedon had a very long neck comprising 62 vertebrae, measuring about 5.9 meters or over half its total body length.
facts.quote: The neck is also very long; it comprises 62 vertebrae and is about 5.9 m - over half of the total length.

facts.statement: The skull of Thalassomedon was 47 centimeters long and contained teeth that were 5 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The skull is 47 cm long, with 5 cm long teeth.

facts.statement: The flippers of Thalassomedon measured between 1.5 and 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: The flippers were about 1.5 – 2 m long.

facts.statement: Stones found in the stomach area of Thalassomedon led to theories that they were used for ballast or to aid digestion.
facts.quote: Stones have been found in its stomach area leading some to theorize that they were used for ballast or digestion.

facts.statement: Thalassomedon belongs to the family Elasmosauridae and its closest relative is Elasmosaurus.
facts.quote: Its closest relative is Elasmosaurus, and both belong to the family Elasmosauridae.

facts.statement: Six specimens of Thalassomedon in varying states of preservation are displayed in museums across the United States.
facts.quote: There are six specimens of varying states of preservation on display at various museums in the United States.

facts.statement: Thalassomedon is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
This genus of plesiosaur appeared in North America about 95 million years ago.
facts.quote: Este género de plesiosaurio apareció en Norteamérica hace cerca de 95 millones de años.

facts.statement: Thalassomedon had a body length of 12 meters, with a neck spanning 62 vertebrae representing half the animal's length (6 meters).
facts.quote: Con una longitud corporal de 12 metros, el cuello abarca 62 vértebras que representan la mitad de la longitud del animal (6 metros).

facts.statement: The time range for Thalassomedon is the Cenomanian, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Thalassomedon lived in North America approximately 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
rejected.quote: This genus of plesiosaur lived in North America, approximately 95 million years ago - this places it during the Cenomanian stage.
